label: input token p during the original phase
explanation: Token detector for p: fires whenever p is input as an original token (t < L), at every position and for every L, with precision 1.0 on dev. It does not fire on p when the model feeds p back in during the copy phase, apart from a tiny residue (271 dev steps, almost all at recall_idx 1). It never fires on any other token or on <DEL>. Magnitude is highest (around the max, 3.0) for p at t=0. In the examples, it is lower for p later in the sequence and for a repeat p (around 0.4-0.9 of max). Neither L nor the neighbouring tokens change whether it fires.

issues: None of the issues are material. On test: precision 1.0, recall 0.997, F1 0.999, mass recall 0.9999. There are zero false positives on test.

The 300 test misses are the copy-phase p residue the explanation already mentions. All of them are the first fed-back token (recall_idx 1) in sequences that start with p. Each fires at only 0.01-0.06 of max and together they hold 0.0% of the activation mass, so this is near-zero leakage rather than a separate case the label misses.

The dev profile confirms the other claims. Activity is 0 on <DEL> and 0 on every token other than p. The rate is flat across L (0.017) and across the previous token. Per-original-position rate is a constant 0.033, roughly 1/30, which is p's base frequency. Top activations (1.00) are p at t=0. The examples show p lower later in the sequence (about 0.54-0.92) and a repeated p lower still (about 0.37-0.6), which matches the explanation.
